learnerActions: Compare your response with the sources
Highlight copied strings, paraphrases, summaries and your own comment in different colours
Revise one section to reduce reliance on source wording
activities.intendedInsight: Source language can support writing, but it must be transformed and attributed.
activities.rationale: Plakans and Gebril found that writers drew on sources for language support as well as content; making this use visible allows it to be managed rather than hidden.

difficulties.pattern: I summarise the reading, then I summarise the lecture.
difficulties.revealedBy: Responses organised by source rather than by the relationship the task asks for
difficulties.response: Plan by points of relationship using a planning grid that requires links between sources.

difficulties.pattern: I ran out of time, so I copied.
difficulties.revealedBy: Copied strings concentrated towards the end of responses
difficulties.response: Practise time allocation and condensed note-making that does not reproduce full sentences, then summarise from notes.

difficulties.pattern: I missed the lecturer's main point.
difficulties.revealedBy: Responses that omit or misrepresent the listening input
difficulties.response: Practise lecture note-taking focused on structure and on markers of stance and contrast.

diagnostic.task: Set a short integrated task with one reading and one lecture extract that disagree.
diagnostic.strongResponse: Explains the relationship, uses both sources accurately and selectively, transforms language and is organised by points.
diagnostic.partialResponse: Covers both sources but summarises them separately or borrows phrasing.
diagnostic.gapResponse: Uses only one source or copies extensively.

guidance.contextNotes: Integrated tasks feature in foundation and pre-sessional assessment and in some proficiency tests (see tst.integrated-test-tasks). For undergraduates, the same process underlies source-based coursework, so emphasise transfer from assessment tasks to real assignments.

authorNotes: inf.source-types and inf.scholarly-communication overlap on output types (journals, monographs, grey literature). I scoped source-types as classification by function and readership and scholarly-communication as the production process (peer review, versions, preprints), with source-types as a soft prerequisite of scholarly-communication. inf.source-types is the domain's only entry point.
inf.research-question (focusing a topic for searching) overlaps with res.research-questions. I recommend res.research-questions depend on inf.research-question, not the reverse.

inf.search-records overlaps with ntk.notes-from-reading (full source details in notes) and dig.reference-managers. I did not link them, to avoid guessing other groups' directions; suggested direction: dig.reference-managers depends on inf.search-records.
Cycle risk for the integrator: inf.citation-chaining has cit.referencing-systems as a soft prerequisite. The CIT group should not make cit.referencing-systems depend on inf.citation-chaining.

inf.problematic-publishing touches gai.verifying-output (fabricated references) and pub.journal-selection (choosing where to publish). Suggest both may depend on inf.problematic-publishing or inf.source-evaluation; no edge in the reverse direction should be added.

src.source-functions overlaps with cit.why-cite and cit.citation-functions. Suggested split: cit.why-cite = reasons the academy requires citation (credit, verifiability); src.source-functions = writer-facing choice of what a source will do in one's own argument; cit.citation-functions = analytic taxonomy of citation functions. Recommend cit.citation-functions depend on src.source-functions, not the reverse.

src.signal-phrases, src.reporting-verbs and grm.reporting-structures overlap. I treated grm.reporting-structures as the grammatical prerequisite of src.signal-phrases, and src.signal-phrases as the prerequisite of src.reporting-verbs (basic frames before stance-bearing verb choice). The GRM group should not make grm.reporting-structures depend on any src topic.

src.patchwriting is placed after src.paraphrasing (hard) and int.plagiarism (soft): the concept is recognised against the target of acceptable paraphrase. The paraphrasing mastery evidence asks learners to judge closeness without requiring the term. The INT group should not make int.plagiarism depend on src.patchwriting; int.similarity-reports could reasonably depend on src.patchwriting.

Cycle risks for the integrator (my topics depend on these; their owners must not depend back on the named src topic): cit.when-to-cite (src.quoting, src.paraphrasing, src.signal-phrases); cit.author-date-in-text (src.citation-forms, src.secondary-citation); cit.reference-list (src.secondary-citation, src.multilingual-sources); sen.quotation-punctuation (src.quoting); rds.writer-stance (src.reporting-verbs); sta.averral-attribution (src.voice-boundaries); int.plagiarism (src.patchwriting).

Topics I expect to depend on this domain: par.integrating-evidence (on src.integrating-quotations and src.voice-boundaries), ntk.notes-from-reading (on src.paraphrasing or src.summarising-passage), ges.summary-response and ges.annotated-bibliography (on src.summarising-text), cit.locators (on src.quoting), cit.disciplinary-citation (on src.citation-forms and src.reporting-verbs), sta.authorial-voice (could depend on src.voice-boundaries).

src.quoting and sen.quotation-punctuation: I chose punctuation mechanics as the more foundational (hard prerequisite). If the SEN group instead treats quotation punctuation as following quoting, one of the two edges must be dropped.

No topic covers accurately reporting quantitative findings from sources (effect sizes, percentages, sample descriptions) in summary and synthesis; num.interpreting-statistics covers comprehension only. Consider a topic or an explicit scope note in src.summarising-text.

syn.thematic-grouping and syn.gaps-tensions overlap with rdc.literature-mapping (themes, debates, key authors). I treated rdc.literature-mapping as the reading-side overview and made it a soft prerequisite of syn.gaps-tensions only. The RDC group should not make rdc.literature-mapping depend on syn.gaps-tensions; depending on syn.thematic-grouping would be acceptable.

syn.synthesis-matrix is placed before syn.thematic-grouping (soft): teacher-set columns scaffold independent theme generation. I did not add a direct syn.synthesis-concept -> syn.thematic-grouping edge because it is implied through the matrix.

syn.integrated-tasks overlaps with tst.integrated-test-tasks, ges.summary-response and wpr.reading-to-write. I made wpr.reading-to-write a soft prerequisite of syn.integrated-tasks; the WPR group should therefore not make wpr.reading-to-write depend on syn.integrated-tasks. Suggest tst.integrated-test-tasks depend on syn.integrated-tasks.

Cross-strand prerequisites used in SYN whose owners must not depend back on the named syn topic: ntk.notes-from-reading (syn.synthesis-matrix), rdc.reading-for-writing (syn.thematic-grouping), rdc.multiple-texts (syn.relating-sources), par.topic-sentences (syn.synthesis-paragraphs), ntk.lecture-notes (syn.integrated-tasks).

Downstream topics expected to depend on SYN: ges.literature-review-assignment and res.literature-review (on syn.synthesis-paragraphs and syn.thematic-grouping), res.gap-niche (on syn.gaps-tensions), sem.building-on-others could soft-depend on syn.relating-sources for oral synthesis.
syn.gaps-tensions uses cefrEnd C2 because identifying significant gaps continues to develop into expert research performance.
